corrected_value.authors: Riccucci, N. M., G. G. Van Ryzin, and H. Li.
corrected_value.title: Representative Bureaucracy and the Willingness to Coproduce: An Experimental Study.

decisions.quote:
The purpose of this study is to conceptually replicate an earlier study by Riccucci,

Van Ryzin, and Li (2016), who examined the effects of representative bureaucracy on
the public’s willingness to participate with government in recycling. They found that

increased representation of women in the agencies responsible for recycling increased

the likelihood that women would recycle.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly state that the purpose of their study is to conceptually replicate Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016) (DOI: 10.1111/puar.12401), repeatedly referring to it as 'the original study by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016)' (lines 429-431, 640-642) and directly adapting its three-arm name-manipulation design (0%, 50%, and 100% female official names) and willingness-to-coproduce framework. By contrast, the shipped original, Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Lavena (2014) (DOI: 10.1093/jopart/muu006), is discussed only as background literature (lines 87-89, 174-200) on a 2x2 policing legitimacy experiment and is not the study re-tested here.

decisions.quote:
The present study, therefore, seeks to replicate the representative bureaucracy experi-

ment by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016), but using a different policy context:

emergency preparedness. Thus, the present study can be characterized as a concep-

tual replication or conceptual extension, rather than a direct or exact replication

(Makel, Plucker, and Hegarty 2012; Tsang and Kwan 1999).
decisions.reason: The study collects new experimental survey data from 604 US respondents in May 2015 to conceptually re-test the symbolic gender representation finding of Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016) in the domain of emergency preparedness, making it a replication.

decisions.quote:
Thus, whether combined or separately, male

and female participants were not influenced in any statistically significant way by the

variation in first names of Citizens Corps officials. Our experiment, in sum, produced

only null findings, in contrast to the original study by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li

(2016).
decisions.reason: With the tested original study resolved to Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016), the authors' explicit overall verdict is that their conceptual replication produced only null findings across all outcomes (willingness to donate time, money, and blood) and analytic models, in direct contrast to the positive symbolic representation effects reported in the original study. Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'failed'.

decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. The paper explicitly conducts a conceptual replication of the three-arm survey experiment by Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Li (2016; Public Administration Review 76(1): 121–130, doi:10.1111/puar.12401), randomly varying the gender of four officials' first names across all-male, balanced, and all-female conditions in the emergency preparedness domain and comparing the resulting null OLS and logistic regression estimates against the original's positive female coproduction finding. The sole shipped row (input_row_index 2372, 10.1093/jopart/muu006) is Riccucci, Van Ryzin, and Lavena (2014), a distinct earlier 2x2 policing legitimacy experiment discussed only as background context.
